items.title: Never Causing Distress to Give — A Good Person's Giving Concludes

items.zh: 不損惱他而行惠施。如是五相，是名菩薩善士所行名善士施。
items.en: Giving without causing distress to another. ... These five marks are called a bodhisattva's giving as a genuinely good person.

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切種施？

items.title: Section: Giving Complete in Every Kind — Thirteen Marks

items.zh: 當知此施有十三相。一、無依施，二、廣大施，三、歡喜施，四、數數施，五、田器施，六、非田器施，七、一切物施，八、一切處施，九、一切時施，十、無罪施，十一、有情物施，十二、方土物施，十三、財穀物施。
items.en: This giving should be understood as having thirteen marks: giving without dependence on fame, praise, or any return; broad, expansive giving; joyful giving; repeated giving; giving to a worthy field; giving to one that is not; giving every kind of object; giving in every place; giving at every time; giving free of any fault of origin; giving sentient objects; giving local specialties; and giving wealth and grain.

items.zh: 如是十三種相，當知是名菩薩一切種施。云何菩薩遂求施？當知此施有八種相。

items.title: Section: Giving That Fulfils Exactly What Is Asked — Eight Kinds

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，匱乏飲食而求乞者，施以飲食；匱乏車乘而求乞者，施以車乘；匱乏衣服而求乞者，施以衣服；匱乏嚴具而求乞者，施以嚴具；匱乏種種資生什物而求乞者，施以種種資生什物；匱乏種種塗飾香鬘而求乞者，施以種種塗飾香鬘；匱乏舍宅而求乞者，施以舍宅；匱乏光明而求乞者，施以光明。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards one lacking food who asks, give food; towards one lacking a vehicle, give a vehicle; towards one lacking clothing, give clothing; towards one lacking ornaments, give ornaments; towards one lacking everyday goods, give everyday goods; towards one lacking perfume and garlands, give perfume and garlands; towards one lacking housing, give housing; towards one lacking light, give light.

items.zh: 如是八相，是名菩薩遂求施。云何菩薩此世他世樂施？

items.title: Section: Giving That Brings Joy in Both This Life and the Next — Nine Marks Across Three Kinds

items.zh: 當知此施略有九相。謂財施、無畏施、法施，總說名為能令眾生此世他世樂施。
items.en: This giving should be understood as, in brief, nine marks: material giving, giving freedom from fear, and giving the teaching, together called giving that brings beings joy in both this life and the next.

items.zh: 財施者，謂以上妙清淨如法財物而行惠施。調伏慳悋垢而行惠施，調伏積藏垢而行惠施。調伏慳悋垢者，謂捨財物執著。調伏積藏垢者，謂捨受用執著。無畏施者，謂濟拔師子、虎狼、鬼魅等畏，拔濟王賊等畏，拔濟水火等畏。法施者，謂無倒說法、稱理說法，勸修學處。
items.en: Material giving means giving fine, clean, lawfully obtained wealth; giving that overcomes the taint of stinginess; and giving that overcomes the taint of hoarding. Giving freedom from fear means rescuing beings from lions, tigers, wolves, and malevolent spirits; from oppressive rulers and bandits; and from flood and fire. Giving the teaching means teaching without distortion, teaching in accordance with genuine principle, and encouraging others to train in its practice.

items.zh: 如是一切總說九相，是名菩薩能令眾生此世他世樂施。此中財施、無畏施及此差別，能令眾生此世安樂；法施及此差別，能令眾生後世安樂。

items.title: Section: Pure Giving Opens — Ten Marks Named

items.zh: 云何菩薩清淨施？當知此施有十種相。一、不留滯施，二、不執取施，三、不積聚施，四、不高舉施，五、無所依施，六、不退弱施，七、不下劣施，八、不向背施，九、不望報恩施，十、不希異熟施。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's pure giving? This giving should be understood as having ten marks: giving without delay; giving free of distorted views; giving without first hoarding resources; giving without an air of superiority; giving without dependence on praise; giving without shrinking back; giving nothing inferior; giving without favoritism; giving without expecting gratitude; and giving without hoping for a resulting reward.

items.title: Section: Never Making a Petitioner Wait, Never Distorting Giving Through Wrong Views

items.zh: 云何不留滯施？謂諸菩薩見來求者正現在前，速疾惠施，不作留滯；非來求者疾望得財，如諸菩薩速希惠施。
items.en: What is giving without delay? Bodhisattvas, seeing a petitioner genuinely present, give swiftly, without delay — the petitioner does not even hope to receive it as quickly as the bodhisattva actually gives it.

items.zh: 云何不執取施？謂諸菩薩不以妄見執取於施。或執此施空無有果，或執殺害而行惠施以為正法，或執唯施極淨圓滿是世出世究竟清淨。
items.en: What is giving free of distorted views? Bodhisattvas do not cling to any distorted view regarding giving — neither the view that giving produces no result at all, nor the view that killing performed as ritual sacrifice counts as legitimate practice, nor the view that giving alone, perfected, already constitutes ultimate purity in both worldly and transcendent terms.

items.zh: 云何不積聚施？

items.title: Section: Never Hoarding Resources to Give in One Grand Gesture

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，不於長時漸漸積集聚多財物，然後頓施。何以故？非諸菩薩現有施物，見來求者正現在前堪能不施；不見不施是稱正理。云何積財而不速施？
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not spend a long time gradually accumulating abundant wealth in order to give it all away at once. Why is this? Bodhisattvas, possessing objects that could be given, seeing a petitioner genuinely present, are never capable of not giving; they never regard withholding as fitting what is right. How, then, could they accumulate wealth while failing to give it swiftly?

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不見積財後方頓施是能生長多福之門。又正觀見若別、若總求者相似，漸施、頓施財物平等，何緣而執福有差別。
又諸菩薩，見積聚施，其施有罪；見隨得施，其施無罪。何以故？若積聚已然後頓施，是則先時有來求者，其數或百而不施與，令生嫌恨，不忍、不信；後有一類或不希求，畜積珍財，強而頓施。是故菩薩不積聚施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas see that giving after hoarding carries fault, while giving as resources are obtained carries none. Why is this? If one hoards and then gives all at once, then earlier petitioners — perhaps a hundred of them — go unaided, giving rise to resentment, intolerance, and mistrust; and later, someone who no longer even wants it may have accumulated wealth forced upon them all at once regardless.

items.title: Section: Never Boastful, Never Swayed by Praise — Worldly Fame Is Like Empty Grain Husks

items.zh: 云何不高舉施？謂諸菩薩，於來求者謙下心施，亦不與他競勝而施，亦不施已而生憍慢。謂我能施，我是施主，餘則不爾。
items.en: What is giving without an air of superiority? Bodhisattvas give to petitioners with a humble mind, never competing with others over who gives more, and never growing arrogant after giving, thinking: I alone am capable of giving, I alone am a true benefactor, unlike everyone else.

items.zh: 云何無所依施？謂諸菩薩不依稱譽聲頌而施。體達世間稱譽聲頌，虛妄分別文字所起，唯是虛音，繫屬妄嚮，譬如世間䅌䴬葉聚。
items.en: What is giving without dependence on praise? Bodhisattvas do not give depending on acclaim or praise. They fully understand that worldly acclaim and praise arise only from distorted conceptual thought and mere words, being nothing but empty sound, bound up with hollow echoes — like a worldly pile of husked, empty grain stalks.

items.title: Section: Never Discouraged by the Highest Standard, Never Second-Rate, Never Playing Favourites

items.zh: 云何不退弱施？謂諸菩薩，施先意悅，施時心淨，施已無悔；聞諸菩薩廣大第一最勝施時，不自輕蔑、恐怖、退弱。
items.en: What is giving without shrinking back? Bodhisattvas feel joy before giving, a clean mind while giving, and no regret after giving; and hearing of bodhisattvas' own broad, supreme, ultimate giving, they do not belittle themselves, nor grow fearful, nor shrink back.

items.zh: 云何不下劣施？謂諸菩薩，於諸施物勤數簡擇，最勝最妙飲食、車乘、衣服等物，持用布施。云何不向背施？謂諸菩薩其心平等，不隨朋黨，於怨親中悲心等施。
items.en: What is giving nothing inferior? Bodhisattvas diligently and carefully select the very finest food, vehicles, clothing, and similar objects to give. What is giving without favoritism? Bodhisattvas hold an equal mind, never falling into partiality, giving with equal compassion towards enemy, friend, and those in between alike.

items.title: Section: Never Expecting Gratitude, Never Giving for a Future Reward — Pure Giving's Final Two Marks

items.zh: 云何不望報恩施？謂諸菩薩悲心、愍心而行惠施，終不於他希望反報，但觀求樂愛火所燒無有勢力性苦眾生，深心悲愍而行惠施。
items.en: What is giving without expecting gratitude in return? Bodhisattvas give from compassion and pity, never expecting anything in return, seeing instead beings burned by the fire of craving pleasure, powerless, their very nature suffering — and, moved by deep compassion, give.

items.zh: 云何不希異熟施？謂諸菩薩修行惠施，終不希望當來所得財寶圓滿、自身圓滿施果異熟，觀一切行性是虛偽，觀大菩提最勝功德。
items.en: What is giving without hoping for a resulting reward? Bodhisattvas, practising giving, never hope for the future ripened result of abundant wealth or a perfected body as giving's own fruit, seeing all conditioned things as fundamentally hollow, and seeing great awakening alone as the truly supreme achievement.

items.title: Section: The Perfection of Giving Concludes — Nine Aspects Complete, the Path to Awakening Secured

items.zh: 由此十相，菩薩所行布施清淨、最極清淨。
items.en: Through these ten marks, a bodhisattva's giving becomes pure, and most supremely pure.

items.zh: 如是菩薩依止九相所行惠施，圓滿施波羅蜜多已，能證無上正等菩提。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, resting on giving practised through these nine aspects, having thereby perfected the perfection of giving, are able to realise unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

blocks.text: The last aspects of giving, and its purity. Fascicle 39 and the perfection of giving end today.
Thirteen marks, including giving without seeking fame or return, broadly, joyfully, repeatedly, to a worthy field.

"To one lacking food, food; lacking a vehicle, a vehicle; clothing, clothing"; and "to one lacking light, light". Master Cháng Bǎi: if the neighbourhood lacks streetlights, the bodhisattva provides them.

Three kinds: **material giving** (clean, lawful wealth, overcoming stinginess and hoarding); **giving freedom from fear** ("rescuing beings from lions, wolves, spirits, oppressive rulers, floods, and fire"); and **giving the Dharma**.

items: **Without delay**: "the petitioner does not even hope to receive it as quickly as it is given."
**Free of wrong views**: neither "giving produces no result" nor "ritual killing is meritorious".
**Without hoarding first**: "giving after hoarding carries fault": earlier petitioners go away empty-handed.
**Without superiority**: "with a humble mind, never competing over who gives more".
**Not dependent on praise**: worldly acclaim "arises only from distorted thought". Master Cháng Bǎi: like empty husks.
**Not shrinking back** before the highest examples of giving.
**Not inferior**: "selecting the very finest" to give.
**Not expecting gratitude**: seeing "beings burned by the fire of craving".
**Not hoping for reward**: "seeing all conditioned things as impermanent".

blocks.text: "Through these ten marks, giving becomes pure, and most supremely pure." "Resting on giving practised through these nine aspects", bodhisattvas perfect the perfection of giving.

A whole fascicle on generosity: not a vague virtue but a discipline, full of judgement about what helps and what harms. Fascicle 40 turns to the perfection of moral discipline, and the bodhisattva precepts.

quiz.q: On the fifth mark, "giving without causing distress to another," what result does Master Cháng Bǎi say follows from giving that distresses one's family?
options: wealth in the future, but frequent illness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if one's relatives are distressed by the giving, one may have wealth later but will often be ill. Venerable Miào Jìng: one does not force a person into distress in order to give to a petitioner.

quiz.q: In giving that fulfils what is asked, what does the bodhisattva give "to one lacking light who asks"?
quiz.why: "Towards one lacking light, give light." Master Cháng Bǎi: if the neighborhood lacks streetlights, the bodhisattva sponsors a few — light is needed, so light is given. Venerable Miào Jìng: "suì" means to accomplish — fulfilling what you ask.

quiz.q: Which three kinds of giving are together called "giving that brings beings joy in both this life and the next"?
options: material giving, giving freedom from fear, giving the teaching
quiz.why: "Material giving, giving freedom from fear, and giving the teaching, together called giving that brings beings joy in both this life and the next." Venerable Miào Jìng: each of the three has three marks, making nine.

quiz.q: Giving freedom from fear includes "rescuing beings from rulers and bandits." How does Master Cháng Bǎi comment on "rulers"?
options: in fact a king is another kind of bandit — harsh government is fiercer than a tiger
quiz.why: "Giving freedom from fear means rescuing beings from lions, wolves, and malevolent spirits; from oppressive rulers and bandits; and from flood and fire." Master Cháng Bǎi: in fact a king is another kind of bandit — harsh government is fiercer than a tiger.

options: seeing a petitioner present, give swiftly — faster than the petitioner even hopes
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, seeing a petitioner genuinely present, give swiftly, without delay — the petitioner does not even hope to receive it as quickly as the bodhisattva actually gives it." Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva makes no difficulty at all, giving faster than the petitioner hopes.

quiz.q: Worldly praise is likened to a "pile of 䅌 and 䴰." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain these two characters?
options: "䅌" is the wheat stalk, round and hollow; "䴰" is broken wheat husk or chaff
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "䅌" is the wheat stalk — round and empty inside; "䴰" is broken wheat husk or chaff. "Bound up with hollow echoes" is like an echo in an empty valley.

quiz.q: The chapter's conclusion: having perfected the perfection of giving through the nine aspects, what are bodhisattvas able to do?
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, resting on giving practised through these nine aspects, having thereby perfected the perfection of giving, are able to realise unsurpassed, perfect awakening." Venerable Miào Jìng: having perfected giving, one realises awakening and becomes a buddha. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that giving is one of the provisions for awakening.
